To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
controlled wrinkling of graphene at nanoscale was achieved by introducing nanoparticles underneath graphene.
controlled wrinkling of single layer graphene (1-Lg) at nanometer scales is achieved by introducing monosized nanoparticles, with size comparable to strain coherence length, under the 1-Lg.
monodisperse NPs, with size comparable to coherence length, induce controlled wrinkling of graphene and the wrinkling fraction can be quantified by Raman and AFM analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the controlled wrinkling of single layer graphene (1-Lg) by introducing monodispersed nanoparticles (NPs) underneath it.
the wrinkling of single layer graphene induced by monodispersed nanoparticles.
the wrinkling of single layer graphene (1-LGs), induced by monodispersive nanoparticles (NPs) with the size comparable to the graphene strain coherence length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

wrinkling of graphene at the nanometer scale can be achieved by introducing monoparticle underneath the 1LG, and the amount of the wrinkling can be quantified by the analysis of the R and 2D Raman peaks.
the wrinkling of 1-LG is induced by monodispersed nanoparticles, with size comparable to strain coherence length, and the amount of wrinkling can be easily quantified by Raman spectroscopy.
the wrinkled fraction of graphene can be quantified by the intensity of the Raman G and G’ bands, and that the wrinkling is controlled by the amount of nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wrinkling can be quantified by the intensity of the Raman features of 1-LG, while the wrinkling fraction can be tuned by the size and density of NPs.
we developed a facile method to control the wrinkling of 1-LG and a quantitative method to characterize the wrinkle fraction.
the wrinkling of the 1LG is a result of a competition between the strain energy stored in the wrinkling of 1LG and the adhesion energy of 1LG to the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Raman spectroscopy can be used for quantitative characterization of wrinkling in the graphene, which is of great importance in many practical applications.
the wrinkling of graphene can be controlled in a predictable and reproducible way.
monodisperse NPs can be used to control the topography of 1-LG at nanoscale.
